errors: The written relations alone do not visibly force the ternary symmetry of the sigma_i; Grothendieck notices this himself and adds rho sigma_i rho^{-1} = sigma_{i+1} in the margin. As first written the list was incomplete.
The relation sigma_0 sigma_1 = tau_inf tau_1 rho = l_0 rho depends on the particular choice of lifts. It is not verified on the page; it is plausible but I have not checked it in coordinates.

The page does not prove that the listed relations are complete. Completeness follows from the extension structure only once the kernel is identified with the free group on the l's, and that is left implicit.

ideas.what: Group of all lifts of the holomorphic and antiholomorphic automorphisms (S3 x Z/2) of P^1 minus 3 points, as an extension of S3 x Z/2 by the free group F2
ideas.modern_name: Extended modular group PGL2(Z) / extended (2,3,infinity) triangle group; F2 = image of Gamma(2) with PGL2(Z)/Gamma(2) = S3 x Z/2
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses the action on Teichmüller groupoids in genus 0 and the role of complex conjugation, but not this explicit presentation

ideas.what: Lifts of complex conjugation as reflections in the sides of the ideal triangle 0,1,infinity; loops l_i as products of adjacent reflections, with l_inf l_1 l_0 = 1 automatic
ideas.modern_name: Reflection group Z/2*Z/2*Z/2 of an ideal triangle containing Gamma(2)-bar with index 2

ideas.what: Presentation Sigma = ((Z/2 x Z/2) * Z/3) / <<[rho, sigma_0][rho^{-1}, tau_0]>> (next page), with an automorphism swapping sigma_0 and tau_0, not compatible with the extension structure
ideas.modern_name: Non-standard one-relator-over-free-product presentation of PGL2(Z); symmetry likely related to outer automorphisms of PGL2(Z) (unsure)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard presentation is PGL2(Z) = D2 *_{Z/2} D3 (classical)

missed.claim: Grothendieck derives by hand a presentation of the 'real' extended orbifold fundamental group of the lambda-line. This is the group needed to include complex conjugation in the genus-0 Galois–Teichmüller picture. Its content is the classical group PGL2(Z), and he does not seem (on these pages) to name it as such. Nothing new mathematically.
missed.quote: on les relève en σ0,σ1,σ∞,ρ,τ0,τ1,τ∞ (sur τ) ... et l∞ l1 l0 = 1 automatiquement
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Only historical: it documents an early 1981 step toward treating complex conjugation inside the genus-0 / GT framework.

deep.surprise_reason: The page derives a presentation of what is the classical extended modular group PGL2(Z), adapted to the S3 x Z/2 symmetry of P^1 minus {0,1,infinity}. The work is correct and careful but routine. The only mildly curious item is on the next page: the presentation over (Z/2 x Z/2)*Z/3 and an automorphism exchanging a holomorphic involution with a reflection.
transcription_corrections: Line 'on les relations σ̇0, σ̇1, σ̇∞, ρ̇, τ̇' should read roughly 'on a les générateurs σ̇0, σ̇1, σ̇∞, ρ̇, τ̇, avec les relations'.
Fifth relation: 'τ̇ commute à σ̇0, σ̇1, σ̇∞ (donc aussi à ρ̇)' — the image has σ̇_3 written loosely for σ̇_∞.
